name: Personal Learning and Development (L&D Tracker)
procedure: 1. Define what you would like to achieve and the motivation to pursue it
2. Discuss and evaluate the required skills to achieve your desired outcome
3. Inventory the target skill(s) and assess your current knowledge/application of each skill
4. Prioritize skills and select skill for development
5. Evaluate and select appropriate training within quarter to support desired outcome
6. Complete training and write Knowledge Sharing 1 Pager
7. Present 1 Pager and save to Knowledge Wiki
8. Compare desired outcome to actual outcome and return to step 4 to continue to pursue desired outcome.
trigger: Own development goal active OR weekly anchor day

name: Team Learning and Development (L&D Tracker)
procedure: 1. Define what you would like to achieve and the motivation to pursue it
2. Discuss and evaluate the required skills to achieve your desired outcome
3. Inventory the target skill(s) and assess your current knowledge/application of each skill
4. Prioritize skills and select skill for development
5. Evaluate and select appropriate team training within quarter to support desired outcome
6. Complete training and write Facilitate Team Retrospective
7. Create Knowledge Wiki
8. Compare desired outcome to actual outcome and return to step 4 to continue to pursue desired outcome.
trigger: Own development goal active OR weekly anchor day

name: Company Compliance Training (L&D Tracker)
procedure: 1. Track Company Compliance Training requirements in KNET, KNET2, and FastCap
2. Complete training
trigger: First working day of month

name: Document Review
procedure: 1. Receive Document (PRFAQ, MBR, 6 Pager)
2. Schedule time to review and provide written feedback
3. Review Document and Document Feedback
4. Communicate feedback (live, email, chime)
trigger: Named signal fires (document arrived, opportunity assigned, inbox threshold, variance logged)

name: Team Introductions and Engagements
procedure: 1. Identify new partner team or PXT stakeholder
2. Communicate interest for introduction and engagement
3. Schedule Team Intro/Engagement Communication Cycle
4. Review Team PRFAQs, MBRs, 6 Pagers, Wikis, and Data
5. Discuss synergies for process improvement
6. Coordinate intake of process improvement opportunities
trigger: First working day of month

name: Innovation Process - Explore Opportunities
procedure: 1. Add new Opportunity Name to row in Opportunity Tracker
2. Provide a brief 1-2 sentence Opportunity Description of the opportunity.
3. Select the Strategic Category for the opportunity
4. Identify the Executive Sponsor for the opportunity
5. Select the Desired Timeframe for the opportunity to be implemented
6. Identify the Owner/Driver for the opportunity (the person completing opportunity deliverables)
trigger: Own development goal active OR weekly anchor day

name: Innovation Process - Evaluate Opportunity
procedure: 1. Document Target 3-7 Use Cases related to opportunity.  Use cases are based on activities in a process and specific scenarios encountered.
2. Document the technologies proposed for this opportunity
3. Define the primary customer impacted by the opportunity
4. Document the flow of activities / steps in the process from start to finish
5. Estimate opportunity benefit (target population with time, cost, quality benefits)
trigger: Named signal fires (document arrived, opportunity assigned, inbox threshold, variance logged)

name: Innovation Process - PRFAQ
procedure: 1. Update the Opportunity Status field to Active - PRFAQ
2. Complete Writing Hub - Writing Like an Companyian (one time training)
3. Reference Writing Hub PRFAQ Site for Template and Instructions
4. Create a PRFAQ document based on PRFAQ Template
5. Who is the customer?
6. What is the problem or opportunity we propose to solve?
7. What is the most important customer benefit?
8. What does the customer experience look like?
9. How do you know what customers need or want?
10. Identify the Business Case & Target Use Case(s)
11. Outline Technology Model - Add Link to Opportunity Tracker
12. Diagram the Customer Experience Workflow
13. Complete Frequently Asked Questions Template
14. Complete Press Release 1 Pager
15. Submit for Steering Committee PRFAQ Review & Proof of Concept Greenlight
trigger: Named signal fires (document arrived, opportunity assigned, inbox threshold, variance logged)

name: Innovation Process - Proof of Concept/Prototype
procedure: 1. Complete Prototype Plan based on Prototype Plan Template
2. Purpose of Prototype
3. Scope of Prototype
4. Prototype Features (e.g., platform, targeted use cases, front end, backend)
5. User Experience Workflow
6. Success Criteria
7. Future Use Cases
8. Build Prototype to Success Criteria
9. Prototype - Instructions for use
10. Prototype Test Results
11. Lessons Learned and Product Assessment
12. Outline Implementation/Development Plan with Resource Type and FTE Requirements for implementation
13. Estimate Annualized Net Benefit if Opportunity implemented
14. Identify possible Risks to completing opportunity implementation and create Mitigation Plan for each risk
trigger: Named signal fires (document arrived, opportunity assigned, inbox threshold, variance logged)

name: Innovation Process - Product Assessment
procedure: 1. Complete Product Assessment Document based on Product Assessment Template
2. Business Scope
3. Technical Scope
4. Prototype Target Use Cases
5. Prototype Success Criteria and Test Results
6. Product Use Cases with Annualized Net Benefit
7. Product Risks and Mitigation Plan
8. Product Stakeholders
9. Assumptions
10. Constraints
11. Dependencies
12. User Experience Workflows
trigger: Named signal fires (document arrived, opportunity assigned, inbox threshold, variance logged)

name: Innovation Process - Initiate New Product/Program
procedure: 1. Cultivate Opportunity with internal/external stakeholders and executive committee approval
2. Update Opportunity Discovery fields (section 3) as needed
3. Update the Weekly Status field
4. Update Opportunity Stage as required opportunity fields are finalized
5. Finalize the Implementation Requirements based on prioritized business requirements and technical model
trigger: Named signal fires (document arrived, opportunity assigned, inbox threshold, variance logged)

name: PDCA Cycle
procedure: 1. Determine a target activity or process area of interest, the "theme" for the activity and a baseline current condition measurement of the activity.
2. Establish a future state target condition measurement for the activity.
3. Propose an experiment or improvement that can be worked on over the next 48 hours.
4. Spend 10-60 minutes working on the proposed experiment/improvement.
5. Meet every 48 hours to measure the current condition and document results of your experiment.

6. If current condition meets target condition for 3 meetings, select a new process area for improvement. if current condition does not meet target condition go to step 4. and propose a new experiment.
trigger: Prior PDCA cycle measurement recorded

name: 6S Email Activity
procedure: 1. When number of inbox emails exceeds 20, identify:
2. Immediate Action
3. Planned Action/Keep Emails
4. Save to Task/Project Email Folder
5. Archive
6. Delete Emails
7. When any email exceeds 90 days, identify:
8. Any action to be taken
9. Save to Task/Project Email Folder
10. Archive
11. Delete
12. Set Rules and Alerts in Microsoft Office
13. If you are creating a rule to move messages to another folder, make sure that you have created the folder before you start to create the rule using File, New, Folder.
14. Find the message that you want to base the rule on in Outlook and select it so that it is highlighted.
15. Click on the Organize button. You will find this on the top taskbar - it is a yellow button made up of lots of squares, or in the Tools menu.
trigger: Fixed anchor day in the week

name: High-value Communication Time-blocking (30-60 minutes)
procedure: 1. Block 60 minutes in the morning (09:00-10:00) and 30 minutes post-lunch (13:00-13:30) for high-value communication.
2. Identify priority stakeholder messages and draft responses deliberately (not reactively).
3. Work key project-related threads in email, Slack, and chat tools that require thoughtful reply.
4. Close outstanding requests and confirm explicit follow-up dates.
5. Log a short outcome note summarizing decisions made or blockers surfaced.
trigger: Same time each work day

name: High-value team and project meetings (15-30 minutes)
procedure: 1. Identify recurring team and project meetings that require attendance this sprint.
2. For each meeting, confirm the agenda and desired outcomes are published in advance.
3. Target 20-minute or 50-minute meetings (respect natural break boundaries).
4. Attend meetings prepared with the relevant context and reference documents.
5. Capture decisions, action items, and owner / due-date assignments in real time.
6. Publish notes to the team within 24 hours and follow up on open commitments.
trigger: Fixed anchor day in the week

name: Connecting with other Companyians (15-60 minutes)
procedure: 1. Identify key stakeholders and peers needing one-on-one engagement this sprint.
2. Schedule 20-minute 1:1 meetings, preferring Wednesdays and Thursdays.
3. Prepare an agenda with 2-3 topics and an explicit desired outcome for the meeting.
4. Conduct the meeting focused on relationship building and information exchange.
5. Capture any action items and commit to a follow-up cadence.
6. Track 1:1 effectiveness: cancellation rate, agenda completeness, outcome clarity.
trigger: Fixed anchor day in the week

name: Document Writing (Backlog, Updates, Blurbs, Narratives)
procedure: 1. Identify the document type (Backlog entry, Status Update, Blurb, Narrative, PRFAQ, MBR).
2. Review the template and instructions specific to that document type.
3. Draft the document in a single focused writing block — no switching.
4. Self-review for clarity, completeness, and data accuracy.
5. Circulate for peer review and incorporate feedback.
6. Publish to the canonical location (Wiki, Tracker, shared drive) and notify stakeholders.
trigger: Fixed anchor day in the week

name: Refining Program Plan
procedure: 1. Open current Program Plan and latest sprint outcomes.
2. Identify gaps: slipped milestones, changed scope, new dependencies, resource shifts.
3. Incorporate stakeholder feedback from last week's 1:1s and reviews.
4. Update milestone dates, owners, and dependency links.
5. Note the diff in a short changelog block.
6. Publish updated plan to team channel.
trigger: Mid-Sprint Review (Fri Wk1) OR program-plan-drift signal

name: DMAIC Project Charter
procedure: 1. Write the problem statement in one paragraph.
2. Document the business case (current cost / risk, expected benefit).
3. Define in-scope and out-of-scope process boundaries.
4. Identify Process Owner, Sponsor, Project Lead, and team members.
5. Set goal statement: baseline X → target Y by date Z.
6. Estimate sprint count (typical DMAIC: 6–8 sprints).
7. Identify top 3 risks and initial mitigations.
8. Obtain Sponsor signature.
9. Register Charter in project portfolio.
trigger: Decision to launch a DMAIC project after Kaizen / variance analysis

name: DMAIC SIPOC
procedure: 1. Type participant names into the SIPOC template.
2. Instruct participants to list 3-7 high-level steps of the process based on their experience.
3. Give participants 10-13 minutes to fill in their responses.
4. Review each step with the team and translate responses into high-level steps (verb + noun).
5. Group similar responses under consolidated process steps.
6. Highlight the final 3-7 process steps on the canvas.
7. Brainstorm Outputs for each process step (1-3 per step in 5-8 minutes).
8. Brainstorm Inputs for each process step (3-7 per step in 5-8 minutes).
9. Brainstorm Suppliers for each input (1-3 per input in 5-8 minutes).
10. Consolidate the unique Suppliers, Inputs, Process Steps, Outputs, and Customers into the Final SIPOC.
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: DMAIC Output Data Collection Plan
procedure: 1. List CTQ output metrics (Y's) from VOC/VOB/VOA.
2. For each metric document: operational definition, unit, method, sampling plan, owner, tool, storage.
3. If measurement risk exists, run MSA (#31) before locking.
4. Pilot DCP for one cycle.
5. Lock DCP and proceed to Baseline (#28).
trigger: Post-SIPOC, before Baseline (#28)

name: DMAIC Stakeholder Analysis
procedure: 1. List all stakeholders impacted by or influencing the project.
2. For each, rate Influence (H/M/L) and Interest (H/M/L).
3. Plot on 2x2 grid; assign quadrant engagement approach.
4. Assign owner per quadrant.
5. Document in Stakeholder Analysis template; feed into Communication Plan.
trigger: DMAIC Charter signed

name: DMAIC Communication Plan
procedure: 1. Copy the four Stakeholder Analysis quadrants into the Comm Plan matrix.
2. For each row define cadence, channel, format, owner.
3. Write an acceptance criterion per row.
4. Book recurring calendar holds for every synchronous touchpoint.
5. Publish and revisit at each Sprint Retrospective.
trigger: Stakeholder Analysis complete

name: DMAIC Risk and Mitigation Plan
procedure: 1. Brainstorm risks in four buckets: technical, organizational, timeline, resource.
2. For each risk rate Probability (1–5) × Impact (1–5).
3. For score ≥ 12 write a mitigation plan and assign a risk owner.
4. For score 6–11 write a monitoring plan.
5. Record in Risk Register template.
6. Review at every Sprint Retrospective.
trigger: Post-Charter; refresh at each Sprint Retrospective

name: DMAIC VOC/VOB/VOA Analysis
procedure: 1. Voice of Customer: interview 3–5 customers.
2. Voice of Business: interview 2–3 business leaders.
3. Voice of Associate: interview 3–5 associates.
4. Translate each raw voice into a CTQ requirement.
5. Prioritize CTQs by frequency, severity, strategic fit.
6. Document and feed into Output DCP (#22) and C&E Matrix (#34).
trigger: Post-Charter

outputArtifact.name: VOC / VOB / VOA Document with CTQs

name: DMAIC Continuous Reporting Framework
procedure: 1. Define reporting cadence (weekly or monthly).
2. Select metrics: baseline, current, target, delta, trend, sigma, financial.
3. Build dashboard linked to DCP data source.
4. Assign owner and monthly review slot.
5. Publish link per Communication Plan (#24).
trigger: Post-Baseline (#28)

name: DMAIC Baseline Output Performance Data
procedure: 1. Execute DCP for baseline period (30 working days or 30 samples).
2. Collect data per plan; log deviations.
3. If manual measurement, verify with MSA (#31).
4. Compute summary statistics: n, mean, median, stdev, min, max, Cp/Cpk, sigma.
5. Build baseline Control Chart (#29).
6. Record baseline value in Charter as locked reference.
trigger: Output DCP locked

name: DMAIC Control Chart Graph
procedure: 1. Open the statistical tool (Minitab, JMP, or equivalent).
2. Navigate to Stat > Control Charts > Variables Charts for Subgroups > Xbar.
3. Complete the dialog box with the subgroup data and column references.
4. Click Xbar Options, then open the Tests tab.
5. Select "1 point > K standard deviations from center line" and enter 2.5.
6. Select "K points in a row on same side of center line" and "K points in a row within 1 standard deviation of center line (either side)".
7. Click OK in each dialog box to generate the Xbar chart with 2.5σ control limits.
8. Review the chart for out-of-control points and document findings in the DMAIC workbook.
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: DMAIC Process Capability Report
procedure: 1. Verify data normality (histogram + Anderson-Darling).
2. Define spec limits (USL / LSL).
3. Calculate short-term capability: Cp, Cpk.
4. Calculate long-term performance: Pp, Ppk.
5. Compute DPMO and process sigma.
6. Flag if Cpk < 1.33.
trigger: Baseline data locked

name: DMAIC MSA Report
procedure: 1. Select 10 samples covering the expected process range.
2. 2–3 appraisers measure each sample 2–3 times randomized.
3. Compute Gage R&R (repeatability + reproducibility).
4. Acceptance: <10% excellent; 10–30% marginal; >30% unacceptable.
5. If unacceptable, fix and re-run MSA.
6. Document results and decision.
trigger: Output DCP drafted; before locking

name: DMAIC Detailed Process Maps
procedure: 1. Complete high level process map (SIPOC)
2. Detail 3-7 key sub-processes
3. Estimate process times and wait times
4. Define the inputs and outputs for each step
5. Identify all steps in the process as value added and non-value added
6. Identify 1-3 relevant measurement opportunities for each sub-process
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: DMAIC Quick Win Improvements
procedure: 1. Filter: lead < 1 week AND cost < $1K AND effort < 2 pd AND reversible.
2. Get Process Owner approval.
3. Implement change.
4. Measure impact before and after (≥ 5 observations each).
5. Log: name, hypothesis, delta, decision.
6. Feed kept wins into Improvement Backlog (#38).
trigger: Quick-win candidate identified (lead < 1w, cost < $1K, effort < 2 person-days)

name: DMAIC Cause and Effect Matrix/Analysis
procedure: 1. List every unique Input from the SIPOC down the Cause & Effect matrix rows.
2. List every unique Output from the SIPOC across the matrix columns.
3. Explain the purpose of Cause & Effect Analysis to the project team.
4. Rate each Input against each Output on a 0, 1, 4, 9 scale.
5. Review and align with the team on the final input-to-output ratings.
6. Rate the importance of each Output to the customer on a 1-10 scale.
7. Compute the weighted score for each Input (sum of rating × output-importance).
8. Prioritize Inputs by weighted score; the top-ranked Inputs flow into the FMEA.
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: DMAIC Inputs Data Collection Plan
procedure: 1. Take top-scored X variables from C&E Matrix (4–6 inputs).
2. For each X document: operational definition, method, sampling plan, owner, tool.
3. For each X-Y pair confirm the time-stamp join key.
4. If any X is subjective/manual, run MSA (#31) for that X.
5. Pilot for one cycle; fix and re-pilot if n < 80%.
6. Lock the Input DCP.
7. Execute for min 30 paired X-Y observations.
trigger: Post-C&E Matrix, before Correlation / Regression (#36)

name: DMAIC Correlation and Regression
procedure: 1. Load paired X and Y data.
2. Pairwise correlation matrix; note |r| > 0.4.
3. Fit regression; escalate as diagnostics warrant.
4. Check R² (> 0.7), p-values (< 0.05), residual plots.
5. Identify vital few X's.
6. Document model and leverage points.
7. Feed vital X's into FMEA (#37).
trigger: Input DCP data collected (min 30 paired observations)

name: DMAIC Failure Modes Effects Analysis
procedure: 1. Bring the prioritized Inputs from the Cause & Effect Analysis into the FMEA template.
2. Explain the purpose and scoring rules of each FMEA column to the team.
3. Give participants 15-20 minutes to identify failure modes, effects, root causes, and recommended actions for each Input in their own tab.
4. As a team, review Column B (failure modes) for each Input and remove duplicates.
5. Discuss Column C (customer impact) for each failure mode and capture responses.
6. Review Column D (root causes), remove duplicates, and clarify as needed.
7. Identify Column E (current controls) preventing each failure.
8. Review Column F (improvement actions); bold the ones the team commits to work.
9. Transfer the bolded improvement actions to the Improvement Backlog.
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: DMAIC Process Improvement Backlog
procedure: 1. Aggregate improvement candidates from FMEA, Quick Wins pending, VOC gaps, retro actions.
2. For each: name, one-sentence description, Day-2-Done criteria, effort, impact.
3. Score priority (RICE / WSJF / Impact × Confidence ÷ Effort).
4. Publish prioritized list to Sprint Planning.
5. Carry unfinished items forward.
trigger: Post-FMEA or at each sprint boundary

name: DMAIC Financial Benefit Translator
procedure: 1. Identify benefit categories: hard-dollar, revenue lift, quality/rework, risk avoidance.
2. Quantify current cost / loss per period at baseline.
3. Project post-improvement cost / loss at target.
4. Compute annualized net benefit = 12 × monthly delta.
5. Apply confidence rating: Hard / Soft / Cost Avoidance.
6. Obtain Finance-partner sign-off.
7. Register in portfolio benefits ledger.
trigger: Baseline complete (projection) OR post-improvement (actual)

name: DMAIC Implemented Improvements
procedure: 1. Open Current Failure Modes Effect Analysis spreadsheet
2. Review each recommended action for improvement of process inputs
3. Identify Improvement Backlog Item(s)
4. Document Improvement Backlog Item(s) Name, Description, and Day 2 Done Criteria
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: DMAIC Project Results Narrative Document
procedure: 1. Executive summary: problem → result → annualized benefit.
2. Background: business case, scope, goal.
3. Results: baseline vs remeasured, Control Chart before/after.
4. Root cause findings: vital X's, FMEA failure modes addressed.
5. Implemented improvements with before/after.
6. Financial benefit with confidence.
7. Control plan: ongoing monitoring, SOPs, Process Owner.
8. Lessons learned.
9. Review with Sponsor and file in portfolio.
trigger: Control phase complete, Financial Benefit signed off

name: Kaizen Project Charter
procedure: 1. State problem in one paragraph with scope and pain observed.
2. Document business case.
3. Define event scope.
4. Set goal statement: baseline X → target Y by event end + 30 days.
5. Identify event team: Lead, Process Owner, SMEs, Sponsor.
6. Schedule event window.
7. Identify top 3 risks.
8. Obtain Sponsor signature.
trigger: Kaizen candidate approved for event

name: Kaizen Output Data Collection Plan
procedure: 1. List the 1–3 CTQ output metrics from the Kaizen Charter goal.
2. For each metric document: operational definition, method, pre/post sampling plan, owner, tool.
3. If measurement is subjective, run a quick 3-appraiser MSA on 5 samples.
4. Execute pre-event collection on Day 1.
5. Schedule post-event collection at event end + 30 days.
6. Store DCP alongside Charter.
trigger: Event start

name: Kaizen Event Scheduling
procedure: 1. Review the Desired Project Team Roles on Project Charter
2. Select high performing subject matter experts to meet requirements of the team roles
3. Identify general timeframe of window of opportunity and negotiate availability and commitment
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: Kaizen Event SIPOC
procedure: 1. Type participant names into the Kaizen SIPOC template.
2. Instruct participants to list 3-7 high-level steps of the process being kaizened.
3. Give participants 10-13 minutes to respond.
4. Translate responses into consolidated high-level steps (verb + noun).
5. Highlight the final 3-7 process steps.
6. Brainstorm Outputs for each process step (1-3 per step in 5-8 minutes).
7. Brainstorm Inputs for each process step (3-7 per step in 5-8 minutes).
8. Brainstorm Suppliers for each Input.
9. Consolidate Suppliers, Inputs, Steps, Outputs, and Customers into the Final SIPOC.
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: Kaizen Event Prioritized Inputs
procedure: 1. List every unique Input from the Kaizen SIPOC as rows.
2. List every unique Output from the Kaizen SIPOC as columns.
3. Explain Cause & Effect scoring (0, 1, 4, 9) to the team.
4. Rate each Input against each Output and align as a team.
5. Rate each Output's importance to the customer on a 1-10 scale.
6. Compute the weighted score per Input.
7. Select the top-priority Inputs to move into the Kaizen FMEA.
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: Kaizen Event Failure Modes Effects Analysis
procedure: 1. Carry the prioritized Inputs from the Prioritized Inputs step into the Kaizen FMEA template.
2. Explain the FMEA column scoring rules to the team.
3. Give participants 15-20 minutes to identify failure modes, effects, root causes, and recommended actions per Input.
4. Consolidate duplicate failure modes as a team.
5. Capture customer impact for each failure mode.
6. Review and consolidate root causes.
7. List current controls that prevent each failure.
8. Bold the improvement actions the team commits to executing during the event.
9. Transfer committed actions to the Kaizen Improvement Backlog.
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: Kaizen Implemented Improvements
procedure: 1. Open Current Failure Modes Effect Analysis spreadsheet
2. Review each recommended action for improvement of process inputs
3. Identify Improvement Backlog Item(s)
4. Document Improvement Backlog Item(s) Name, Description, and Day 2 Done Criteria
trigger: Prior step in project / event chain complete

name: Kaizen project Results Narrative 3 Pager
procedure: 1. Page 1 — Problem & Goal: statement, baseline, goal, team, dates, owner.
2. Page 2 — What Was Done: improvements, before/after diagrams, C&E/FMEA insights.
3. Page 3 — Results: remeasured metric, delta, secondary metrics, financial benefit, lessons.
4. Publish to Kaizen portfolio.
trigger: Post-remeasurement (event + 30 days)

name: Kaizen Process Owner Transition
procedure: 1. Walk Process Owner through each implemented improvement and its performance vs baseline.
2. Confirm control measures: updated SOP, Control Chart thresholds, rollback plan.
3. Transfer ownership of ongoing monitoring.
4. Schedule 30/60/90-day Process Owner check-ins.
5. Both parties sign; file with Kaizen record.
6. Kaizen Lead steps back.
trigger: Kaizen Results Narrative complete AND remeasured metric captured

name: Quarterly Planning
trigger: First working day of each quarter
procedure: 1. Review prior quarter: OKR confidence vs actual, Kaizens closed with validated benefit, sprint-goal completion rate.
2. Align to org priorities and externally imposed constraints for the coming quarter.
3. Draft quarterly OKRs (3–5).
4. Lay out 6 sprints + 1 reset sprint (Sprint 7) on the calendar.
5. Allocate Kaizen portfolio across sprints.
6. Identify Sprint 7 reset scope.
7. Publish to team, schedule Sprint 1 Planning.

name: Sprint Planning
trigger: Mon Wk1 of sprint, 09:30 local
procedure: 1. Phase 1 (1h): Team selects Improvement Backlog items it commits to turning into fully documented improvements.
2. Phase 2 (1h): Team decomposes selected items into tasks with estimates and assignments.
3. Output: Sprint Backlog that reflects mutual commitment.

name: Daily Standup
trigger: Same time each work day, 09:00 local
procedure: 1. Each member answers three questions: what have you done, what will you do next, what impedes you?
2. No side conversations; 15 minutes hard stop.
3. Post-standup side-meetings scheduled for interested parties.

name: Mid-Sprint Review
trigger: Fri Wk1 of sprint, 15:00 local
procedure: 1. Team reviews sprint progress vs commitment.
2. Identify any items that should move out of sprint or be deferred.
3. Confirm plan for Wk2.

name: Sprint Review
trigger: Fri Wk2 of sprint, 14:00 local
procedure: 1. Team presents sprint goal, committed backlog, completed backlog.
2. Members demonstrate completed improvements.
3. Stakeholders polled for feedback + priority changes.
4. Process Owner discusses backlog rearrangement.

name: Sprint Retrospective
trigger: Fri Wk2 of sprint, 15:00 local (immediately after Review)
procedure: 1. Team answers: what went well; what could be improved?
2. Facilitator captures in summary form.
3. Prioritize improvements; add high-priority items to next sprint backlog.

name: Deep Work — Project Task (generic)
trigger: PROJECT bucket has slack and no DMAIC/Kaizen payload eligible
procedure: 1. Declare intention for the block.
2. Work the primary project task uninterrupted.
3. At close, log output and any friction.

name: Value-Added Communication (generic)
trigger: COMMUNICATION bucket has slack and no named comm entry eligible
procedure: 1. Triage inbox / chat / calendar for value-added touchpoints.
2. Respond deliberately (not reactively).
3. Log a short outcome note at close.

name: End-of-Activity Reflection
trigger: Close-of-day reflection anchor, 17:00 local
procedure: 1. Scan the day's closed activities.
2. Note what went well.
3. Note what to improve.
4. Flag any friction signals for the Kaizen queue.

name: Weekly Reflection
trigger: Friday afternoon, 16:30 local
procedure: 1. Define: what was the dominant pain pattern this week?
2. Measure: baseline rough count or duration.
3. Analyze: candidate causes.
4. Improve: promote at most one candidate to a Kaizen.

name: Lessons Learned
trigger: Every Kaizen close (every projectType, every closeKind)
procedure: 1. What worked — improvements that beat baseline.
2. What didn't — improvements abandoned or reverted.
3. Next to try — hypotheses for the next iteration.
4. Publish alongside the Kaizen record.
